words.gloss: to those who do not let go

literal: Grasping and not leaving, miseries [will grasp] those who, grasping attachment, do not let go.
translation: Sufferings will cling to and never let go of those who hold fast to their attachments and refuse to renounce them.
modern: பற்றுகளைப் பிடித்துக்கொண்டு அவற்றை விடாதவர்களை, துன்பங்கள் விடாமல் பற்றிக்கொள்ளும்.
explanation: This couplet uses a powerful wordplay on 'grasping' (பற்று) to illustrate the law of cause and effect in attachment. Just as a person holds onto worldly desires and refuses to let them go, sufferings will likewise grasp that person and refuse to leave. The repetition of 'பற்றி விடாஅ' (grasping and not letting go) for both the seeker's attachment and the resulting misery emphasizes that our pain is a direct mirror of our clinging. True liberation from sorrow is achieved only when we voluntarily release our grip on these attachments.
